records.supported_name_scope: Guadalupe River is supported as the representative identity of the two-piece Texas corridor. The western approach corresponds to the North Fork before the river continues through Kerrville, the Canyon Reservoir setting, New Braunfels, Gonzales and Victoria toward the San Antonio Bay estuary. Initial feeder details, impoundment passages and terminal distributary names are not assigned one uniform hydronym.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The actual complete west-to-east upper course, Kerrville-area southeast bend, Canyon-area southward turn, eastward middle reach, renewed southern course and southeast coastal ending were compared with readable original TPWD and Guadalupe-Blanco River Authority maps. Texas is an editorial geographic qualifier.
records.region: Texas, United States: western Kerr County through the Hill Country and Gulf Coastal Plain to the San Antonio Bay estuarine setting.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded representative-system correspondence for both selected fragments. The retained statewide original, acquired Kerr County map and acquired whole-basin poster provide sufficient visual correspondence. Exact initial feeder, impoundment limits and coastal distributary or mouth naming remain outside this completed scope. No further acquisition is pending.

naming_scope_details.upper_scope: North Fork Guadalupe River is the supported western approach. The headmost feeder and exact North Fork-to-Guadalupe transition vertex remain unassigned. South Fork and Johnson Creek are separate branches.
naming_scope_details.reservoir_scope: Canyon Reservoir and the smaller downstream impoundment settings remain distinct waterbodies. No present water level, dam condition or coordinate-exact reservoir boundary is inferred.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: Comal, San Marcos, Coleto Creek and San Antonio are separate contributing corridors. The two selected pieces are modeled mainstem fragments, not proof that all connected waterways share one name.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: The Guadalupe-to-San Antonio Bay estuarine association is supported. Individual distributary names, tidal-channel boundaries, current shoreline and exact mouth remain unassigned; no open-Gulf river extension is asserted.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The model's mainstem roles and display length do not establish a uniform natural-river name, surveyed source-to-mouth length or present flow. Fragment joins are not naming boundaries. Historical recreation and ecological-condition statements are not adopted as current advice.

records.supported_name_scope: Altamaha River supports the representative identity of this connected river group. Its upper Oconee-side corridor, western Ocmulgee contribution, impoundments and tidal branches retain separate names and scope; Altamaha is not a uniform hydronym for all selected coordinates.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The actual three-piece mainstem and two western contributing pieces were compared with the original NOAA basin network, the Gwinnett headwater map, the DNR river guide and direct official text. The headward eastward approach, southward reservoir corridor, separate western river with an eastward lower elbow, two-river junction and southeast coastal trunk support the Altamaha system. Georgia and the word system are editorial scope qualifiers.
records.region: Georgia, United States: the Little Mulberry/upper Oconee setting, Oconee and lower Ocmulgee corridors, and the Altamaha coastal approach near Darien.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded representative-system correspondence using already received independent evidence. Small upstream name-transition vertices and individual estuarine channels are not assigned. Failed optional publications remain stopped; no further material is needed for this bounded identity.

naming_scope_details.geographic_qualifier: Georgia, United States; editorial disambiguation only.
naming_scope_details.upper_scope: Little Mulberry and the upper Oconee contributing network retain separate scope; no surveyed source or exhaustive upstream name sequence is claimed.
naming_scope_details.impoundment_scope: Lake Oconee and the Sinclair impoundment are separate waterbodies within the upper corridor, not river aliases.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: Oconee and Ocmulgee remain distinct contributing rivers; the selected western branch is not renamed Altamaha. Ohoopee is additional neighboring tributary context.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Altamaha coastal and sound setting supported; individual Darien, Champney and other tidal channels are not assigned to the modeled terminal segment.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: Modeled mainstem membership and display length do not establish one official name, natural-river length, surveyed headwater or modern shoreline. No formal naming decision or naming date was verified.

records.supported_name_scope: Winisk River is supported as the representative drainage identity of the seven-piece selection. This is not a uniform hydronym for the modeled southern feeder, lake passages, western contributing lake-chain route or the separate lower Asheweig tributary. The downstream trunk and its Hudson Bay estuarine approach correspond to the mapped Winisk corridor. Fine upper-feeder and lake-transition names remain unassigned.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The full selected network was considered against the readable retained Ontario Geological Survey Northern Sheet: the western lake belt, southern lake-country approach, northern Winisk Lake outlet, northward trunk and its eastward bulge, separate western tributary, pronounced eastward lower-river turn and final northeast estuarine approach. The adjacent Severn, Asheweig, Winiskisti Channel, Shagamu and Sutton features were kept distinct. This is regional cartographic correspondence, not a vertex-level match or a surveyed headwater determination.
records.region: Northern Ontario, Canada, from the Wunnummin–Winisk lake country through the Hudson Bay Lowlands to the Winisk estuary.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded representative-system research using the retained original OGS regional map. Every selected fragment was considered; the original map is generalized and does not resolve the short initial southern feeder or every internal lake passage. Those limits do not prevent the representative Winisk identity. Optional park-source failure does not leave required source material pending. Further local feeder naming would be separately scoped work.

naming_scope_details.upper_scope: The southern modeled mainstem begins upstream of the directly labeled Winisk corridor. Regional lake-country correspondence is supported; the short initial feeder, exact natural headwater and name transitions remain unassigned. Fishbasket and Mameigwess are contextual lake labels, not a claim that every selected upper vertex lies in either lake.
naming_scope_details.lake_scope: Wunnummin and the connecting eastern lake complex, including Winisk Lake, remain lake passages and contributing waters. No lake name is converted into a river alias and no exact internal named-water boundary is assigned.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: The western lake-chain contribution and lower Asheweig contribution remain distinct from the modeled mainstem. The nearby Frog and Muzhikoba labels and Winiskisti Channel are not promoted to whole-group names. The exact beginnings of tributary hydronyms are outside scope.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Hudson Bay estuary correspondence is supported by the continuous mapped Winisk corridor and coast. Exact tidewater, mouth vertex, modern shore and individual estuarine channels are not established.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The seven display fragments and four modeled-mainstem pieces do not define seven natural rivers or four hydronym reaches. Display lengths are not asserted natural river lengths. MAIN_RIV membership, bounding box and nearest labels were not used as sole identity evidence. No formal naming date, Indigenous-name equivalence or translation is asserted.

records.supported_name_scope: No natural river identity is established for the complete modeled Inland Ice path. This completed feature-class and naming-scope hold does not claim that every nearby marginal stream is unnamed.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Northern Greenland Inland Ice, with a long nearly northward interior line and a northern approach into the Victoria Fjord setting. The fjord is geographic and feature-class context, not an assigned river name.
records.completion_scope: Readable coverage supports the completed scope hold. Positive natural-river identity evidence would be required before any later name assignment; no further acquisition is pending now.

naming_scope_details.length_limit: Model display length, not a measured natural-river length.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Keep the saved order unchanged and use later result IDs/status changes to mark progress. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated; no lake research until all river continental phases have had their review pass.
